SEAS quasi-dynamic operator with far-field Dirichlet boundary loading (BP1-style). Couples AntiplaneBdrLoadOperator (domain with far-field Dirichlet BCs) with a BdrLoadFaultAdapter (rate-state fault). Below-Wf fault nodes are prescribed at V=Vp matching Tandem's deep extension Dirichlet BC.
nodes.name: seas_bdrload_operator.hpp

nodes.summary: Adapter for RateStateFaultOperator used with far-field Dirichlet loading. Wraps an existing fault operator and adds BP1-specific behavior: below-Wf nodes are prescribed at V=Vp (plate rate), while above-Wf nodes use standard rate-and-state friction. Template parameter MeshType selects serial (Mesh) or parallel (ParMesh).
nodes.name: class::BdrLoadFaultAdapter

nodes.summary: Initialize fault state from stress equilibrium. For above-Wf nodes: computes initial theta (or psi) from the friction law so that stress balance holds at V_init. For below-Wf nodes: sets slip rate to plate velocity Vp. Returns the maximum slip rate V_max.
nodes.name: function:method::BdrLoadFaultAdapter::Init

nodes.summary: Compute the ODE right-hand side for fault state evolution. Above-Wf nodes: solves the friction law for slip rate V, then computes dslip/dt=V and dtheta/dt from the state evolution law. Below-Wf nodes: prescribed V=Vp, zero state evolution rate. Updates cached slip rate for GetMaxSlipRate() queries.
nodes.name: function:method::BdrLoadFaultAdapter::ComputeRHS

nodes.summary: Verify that the stress balance tau = sigma_n * f(V, theta) + eta * V holds at each above-Wf fault node. Returns the maximum relative error across all nodes. Used to validate initialization.
nodes.name: function:method::BdrLoadFaultAdapter::VerifyStressEquilibrium

nodes.summary: SEAS quasi-dynamic time integration operator for far-field Dirichlet loading (BP1). Inherits from MFEM TimeDependentOperator. Couples the domain solver (AntiplaneBdrLoadOperator) with the BdrLoadFaultAdapter. The Mult() method implements the coupling: extract slip -> solve domain with time-dependent BCs -> compute traction -> compute fault RHS. State vector layout: [slip_0, theta_0, slip_1, theta_1, ...].
nodes.name: class::SEASBdrLoadOperator

nodes.summary: Initialize the state vector at t=0 following Tandem's multi-phase initialization: (1) PreInit with slip=0, (2) domain solve for initial traction, (3) compute theta from stress equilibrium, (4) verify initial slip rate matches V_init within 10%. Asserts stress equilibrium error < 1e-6.
nodes.name: function:method::SEASBdrLoadOperator::SetInitialCondition

nodes.summary: Core ODE right-hand side: (1) extract slip from state, (2) solve domain with slip BC and time-dependent far-field Dirichlet BC, (3) compute traction at fault, (4) compute fault RHS via BdrLoadFaultAdapter. Called by ODE solvers (RK4, Dormand-Prince).
nodes.name: function:method::SEASBdrLoadOperator::Mult

nodes.summary: Primary SEAS quasi-dynamic operator coupling domain solver with fault operator. Supports both antiplane (BP2) and 3D elasticity (BP5) via template parameters. Defines type aliases BP2SEASOp, BP5SEASOp, and PBP5SEASOp for concrete benchmark configurations. Contains v51 debug features for dip traction analysis and elastic normal stress feedback.
nodes.name: seas_operator.hpp

nodes.summary: Central SEAS quasi-dynamic time integration operator. Inherits TimeDependentOperator. Template parameters select mesh type (serial/parallel), domain operator (antiplane/elasticity), and fault operator. Mult() coupling flow: (1) extract slip from state, (2) solve domain problem with slip BC, (3) compute traction on fault, (4) compute fault RHS with slip rate V and dtheta/dt. Supports v51 diagnostic features: zero dip traction, coseismic dip ratio dump, and elastic sigma_n feedback.
nodes.name: class::SEASQuasiDynamicOperator

nodes.summary: Initialize state at t=0 following Tandem's two-phase approach: PreInit (slip=0, theta=placeholder), solve domain for initial traction, compute theta from stress equilibrium, verify initial V_max. For BP5-QD with nucleation overstress, V_max > V_nuc is expected. Uses global MPI reduction for parallel verification.
nodes.name: function:method::SEASQuasiDynamicOperator::SetInitialCondition

nodes.summary: Core ODE right-hand side for time integration. nodes.summary: Adaptive time stepping for SEAS simulations. Contains two classes: AdaptiveTimeStepper (simple slip-rate-based dt control) and DormandPrinceRK45 (embedded RK45 with local error estimation). The DOPRI5(4) integrator is the primary time stepper, modeled after Tandem's PETSc TS configuration with FSAL optimization, PI controller for step size, and MPI-consistent error norm reduction.
nodes.name: time_stepper.hpp

nodes.summary: Simple adaptive time stepper that adjusts dt based on maximum fault slip rate. During interseismic periods (V < 1e-12), uses dt_max (~1 year). During rapid slip (V > V_target), reduces dt proportionally. Otherwise, gradually increases dt by a growth factor. Clamped to [dt_min, dt_max].
nodes.name: class::AdaptiveTimeStepper

nodes.summary: Compute new time step from maximum slip rate using three regimes: very slow slip -> dt_max, rapid slip -> proportional reduction, moderate -> gradual growth. Returns dt clamped to configured bounds.
nodes.name: function:method::AdaptiveTimeStepper::ComputeNewDt

nodes.summary: Dormand-Prince 5(4) embedded Runge-Kutta integrator with adaptive step size control. 7-stage FSAL method where the 5th-order solution advances state and the 4th-order difference provides error estimation. Step size adjusted via PI controller (safety * dt * err^{-1/5}). Supports weighted L-infinity or RMS error norms, MPI-consistent accept/reject, V-guard for CFL safety, NaN detection, and per-stage diagnostics. Matches Tandem's PETSc TS configuration (-ts_rk_type 5dp, -ts_atol 1e-7).
nodes.name: class::DormandPrinceRK45

nodes.summary: Initialize the integrator for a given TimeDependentOperator. Allocates 7 stage vectors (k_[0..6]), temporary solution y_tmp_, and error estimate vector err_. Must be called before first Step().
nodes.name: function:method::DormandPrinceRK45::Init

nodes.summary: Take one adaptive DOPRI5(4) step. Computes 7 RK stages with FSAL reuse, checks for NaN and V-guard violations at each stage, computes weighted error norm (L-inf or RMS), and applies PI controller for next dt. Returns true on acceptance (state and time advanced), false on rejection (dt shrunk with extra reject_safety factor). Contains lambdas compute_max_V, check_v_guard, and diag_rk_stage for stage-level diagnostics.
nodes.name: function:method::DormandPrinceRK45::Step

nodes.summary: Restore FSAL state from checkpoint data. Sets k_[0] and marks the integrator as initialized so the next Step() reuses k_[0] instead of recomputing it.
nodes.name: function:method::DormandPrinceRK45::RestoreFSAL

nodes.summary: Compute L2 norm with NaN-aware parallel reduction. In parallel, checks each rank for NaN locally and broadcasts via GlobalSumInt to ensure all ranks detect the failure consistently. Prevents MPI deadlock from rank-divergent NaN.
nodes.name: function:method::DormandPrinceRK45::NormL2

nodes.summary: Parallel SEAS BP2 driver (main entry point). Runs the full earthquake cycle simulation using MPI. layers.name: Common Utilities

layers.name: Benchmark Configuration
layers.description: Parameter definitions for SCEC benchmark problems BP1, BP2, and BP5 including physical constants and model parameters

layers.name: Domain Operators
layers.description: FEM domain operators implementing antiplane (2D) and elasticity (3D) formulations with DG methods and mesh generation

layers.name: Fault Mechanics
layers.description: Fault geometry, face quadrature, fault basis extraction, and rate-and-state fault coupling

layers.name: Friction Laws
layers.description: Rate-and-state friction implementations including Dieterich-Ruina law and state variable evolution (aging/slip)

layers.name: DG Integrators
layers.description: Discontinuous Galerkin bilinear form integrators: BR2 and IP penalty methods for antiplane and elasticity problems

layers.name: I/O and Output
layers.description: Benchmark output writers, ParaView visualization, checkpoint/restart, and probe data collection

layers.name: Solver and Time Integration
layers.description: SEAS quasi-dynamic operators coupling domain and fault, with adaptive Runge-Kutta time stepping

layers.name: Unit Tests
layers.description: Unit tests for individual components: operators, friction laws, fault mechanics, I/O, and integrators

layers.name: Parallel and Verification Tests
layers.description: MPI parallel consistency tests, scaling tests, and full benchmark verification runs for BP1/BP2/BP5

layers.name: Visualization and Analysis
layers.description: Python scripts for benchmark comparison, result visualization, and mesh convergence analysis

layers.name: Benchmark Data
layers.description: Reference benchmark data from SCEC community codes (Tandem, BinHaoWang, Ozawa, etc.) for verification

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the SEAS miniapp's Claude Code instructions to understand the project's purpose: implementing SCEC SEAS benchmark problems (BP1, BP2, BP5) for earthquake cycle simulation using MFEM's finite element framework. The document outlines the development workflow, reference implementations (Tandem), and debugging practices.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: pseas.cpp is the main parallel SEAS driver that orchestrates the entire earthquake simulation. It initializes MPI, creates the mesh, configures the domain operator and fault, sets up rate-and-state friction, and launches the adaptive time stepper. This file ties together all other components.
tour.languageLesson: C++ header-only design: the SEAS miniapp uses .hpp files that contain both declarations and implementations. This simplifies the build but increases compile times. The #include chain from pseas.cpp pulls in the entire framework.

tour.title: Common Types and MPI Context
tour.description: The foundation layer provides shared type definitions (dimension constants, physical enums), an MPI context wrapper for safe communicator management, and parallel utility functions for reduction operations and data distribution across MPI ranks.

tour.title: Benchmark Parameters
tour.description: Each SCEC benchmark problem (BP1, BP2, BP5) has a dedicated parameter header defining physical constants: fault dimensions, elastic moduli, plate loading rate, friction coefficients (a, b, L, f0, V0), and state evolution law choice. BP5 is the most complex — a 3D strike-slip problem with depth-dependent parameters.

tour.title: Domain Operators
tour.description: The domain operator hierarchy implements the bulk elastic problem. DomainOperator is the abstract interface. AntiPlaneOperator handles 2D scalar (BP1/BP2) using DG-BR2 discretization. ElasticityOperator handles 3D vector elasticity (BP5) with BR2 or IP penalty DG. These operators assemble the stiffness matrix and solve the static equilibrium given fault tractions.
tour.languageLesson: Template-based polymorphism: DomainOperator uses virtual methods for the operator interface while ElasticityOperator (4849 lines) contains the most complex FEM assembly logic, including traction-to-displacement coupling through the fault face.

tour.title: DG Integrators
tour.description: The Discontinuous Galerkin bilinear form integrators implement the numerical flux terms at element interfaces. DGBr2Integrator handles scalar (antiplane) BR2 lifting, DGElasticityBR2Integrator extends this to vector elasticity, and DGElasticityIPPenaltyIntegrator provides an alternative interior penalty formulation.

tour.title: Fault Mechanics
tour.description: Building on the domain operators from Step 5, the fault subsystem manages the earthquake fault interface. FaultGeometry handles fault node identification and coordinate extraction. FaultBasis computes the normal/tangent frame at fault faces. FaceQuadrature provides specialized quadrature for fault face integrals. RateStateFault couples these together to compute fault tractions from slip rate and state variables.

tour.title: Friction Laws
tour.description: The friction subsystem implements rate-and-state friction that governs earthquake nucleation and rupture. FrictionLaw is the abstract interface. DieterichRuina implements the regularized Dieterich-Ruina friction law (tau = sigma_n * a * arcsinh(V/2V0 * exp(psi/a))). StateEvolution provides aging and slip law evolution for the state variable psi.
tour.languageLesson: The friction law uses the regularized form of rate-and-state friction where psi = f0 + b*ln(V0*theta/L) is the compact state variable. This avoids numerical issues with theta->0 that plague the classical formulation.

tour.title: Solver and Time Stepping
tour.description: SEASOperator couples the domain operator with the rate-state fault to form the complete ODE system dy/dt = f(t,y). TimeStepper implements adaptive Runge-Kutta methods (RK45) with error-based step size control. The solver iterates: given current slip and state, solve for displacement, compute traction, update slip rate and state.

tour.title: I/O and Benchmark Output
tour.description: The I/O subsystem handles writing simulation results in formats required by SCEC benchmarks. BenchmarkOutput and BP5BenchmarkOutput write time series of slip rate, slip, and state at specified fault depths. ParaviewOutput exports full-field data for visualization. Checkpoint enables restart from saved state.

tour.title: Tests and Verification
tour.description: The comprehensive test suite validates each component. Unit tests verify individual operators, friction laws, and I/O. Parallel tests check MPI consistency and scaling. Verification tests run full BP1, BP2, and BP5 benchmarks and compare against reference solutions from Tandem and other SCEC community codes.

tour.title: Build System and Infrastructure
tour.description: The CMakeLists.txt and Makefile define build targets for the main driver (pseas), all unit/parallel/verification tests, and mesh generation tools. Job submission scripts automate running simulations on HPC clusters with various mesh resolutions and MPI configurations.
